chapter_title: Chương 175: 0175【Cãi không lại thì chối bai bẻng】

segments.title: Chương 175: 0175【Cãi không lại thì chối bai bẻng】
segments.content:
When Chen Guiliang attended events, he would also run his mouth, but it was always aimed at specific people or companies, and he would stick to the facts without generalizing.

Even when he blasted *Wolf Totem*, he only pointed out the logical errors in the book, one by one. The claim that *Wolf Totem* encouraged traitors and fascists came from other participants later on.

But this Korean was making a sweeping generalization!

The first paragraph the Korean spoke was still somewhat in line with reality.

The plug-ins in web games nowadays were indeed prone to being flagged by antivirus software. That's why *Happy Farm* only had a FlashPlayer plug-in, which was accepted by antivirus software.

He was clearly making a valid point, yet he just had to add the sentence "Chinese people don't understand the internet" at the beginning of his statement.

The beginning of the Korean's second paragraph was even more impressive, starting directly with "Chinese people are very stupid." Even if he stated some facts afterward, it would still infuriate the Chinese people present.

Yangcheng Gnetwork was already sucking up to the Koreans enough as it was, but even they were thoroughly disgusted at this moment.

"Moderator, he gave me the middle finger! He also called me 'Bang Ge'!" Park Heon-joo was getting a little agitated.

The moderator quickly stifled his laughter and reminded Chen Tianqiao, "Mr. Chen, please watch your words and actions."

Chen Tianqiao explained, "Bang means 'awesome,' and ge is a sign of respect. Bang Ge is my honorific for Mr. Park. I believe he has done an outstanding job at Ourgame. As for the middle finger, I'm truly sorry. I've been sending too many text messages recently, and my thumb is extremely tired. I originally wanted to give a thumbs-up and just used my middle finger as a temporary substitute."

The moderator suppressed a laugh and said, "Please be more careful next time. You can't just substitute things randomly."

"Understood. Thank you for the reminder."

After speaking, Chen Tianqiao gave Park Heon-joo a thumbs-up, "Keep it up, Bang Ge!"

Liu Kun of Pixel Soft, who had already stopped laughing, was now tickled into laughter again.

"He's making excuses!"

Park Heon-joo looked at the moderator. "I know what 'bàngzi' means. Someone who used that derogatory term for me has already been fired by me!"

The moderator said, "Mr. Park, Mr. Chen has acknowledged and corrected his mistake. He is no longer giving you the middle finger. There is nothing inappropriate about him giving you a thumbs-up and cheering you on now. Furthermore, he called you 'Bang Ge,' which is a compliment in Chinese. On the contrary, your choice of words just now was very poor."

"Bang!"

"Aishiba!"

Furious, Park Heon-joo slammed the table and stood up.

He had enough confidence to be arrogant because he was the team leader sent to China by NHN.

What was NHN? It was South Korea's largest portal site, search engine, and gaming platform, equivalent to the combination of "Sina, a certain search engine, and QQ Games" in their heyday.

So what if Ourgame had 200 million registered users? So what if Ourgame had servers in China, the US, Japan, and South Korea? The first thing Park Heon-joo wanted to do upon arriving in China was to take down the "Ourgame" brand and replace it directly with NHN's gaming brand, "Hangame." Ourgame's founders strongly opposed this, and it was only dropped after they repeatedly took the issue to NHN headquarters.

He usually dealt with Chinese people from a condescending position.

Now someone was actually giving him the middle finger and using "Bang Ge" to sarcastically allude to "bàngzi."

Chen Tianqiao remained silent with a smile, merely looking at the moderator.

The moderator raised his voice, his tone becoming sterner. "Mr. Park, I must once again remind you to watch your words and actions. Slamming the table and cursing at a roundtable meeting is uncivilized behavior. If you do it again, I have the right to ask you to leave the venue."

Most of the reporters at the summit venue were from print media and websites.

For television media, there was only CCTV Finance and Dragon TV, and their focus was on the main table where Chen Tianqiao and the others were.

As for the other tables, the two television stations just casually swept their cameras over them.

"It looks like there's a situation over there. Let's go take a look," a CCTV reporter said to the cameraman.

With Park Heon-joo slamming the table and standing up to curse, it was hard not to attract attention.

Even the peers at the two adjacent tables stopped their discussions and all looked at the Korean standing there.

Seeing the CCTV camera approaching, Chen Tianqiao shot up to his feet and declared righteously, "Mr. Park, although you are the representative from Korea's largest internet company, please show the Chinese people enough respect. You say Chinese people don't understand the internet, don't understand online games, and I don't want to argue with you about who's right or wrong, but you cannot say that all Chinese people are idiots, that they are all fools!"

Chen Tianqiao's voice was very loud, and even the neighboring tables could hear him.

Everyone's expression turned very ugly.

No one wanted to be called a fool!

Park Heon-joo was originally confronting the moderator. Hearing this, he turned back to Chen Tianqiao, then realized that everyone around was looking at him, and even the television cameras were pointed at him.

He grew a little flustered but was unwilling to lose face, so he sidestepped the cursing issue. "Am I wrong? The most powerful game companies in China right now all got their start by licensing Korean games. More than half of the hottest online games in China right now are Korean games!"

Chen Tianqiao retorted, "Licensing games is not begging for handouts. We split the revenue with the Korean developers. Korean developers earn huge sums from China every year. You should be thanking the Chinese publishers, not insulting Chinese people as fools who can't make games."

"I did not say Chinese people are fools!" Park Heon-joo argued.

Chen Tianqiao asked the moderator, "Then what did he say?"

The moderator said, "His original words were 'Chinese people are very stupid,' and that Chinese game companies should hire Koreans as executives."

"Oh, so that's how it is," Chen Tianqiao asked Wang Zijie, who had just licensed *Audition Online*, "CEO Wang, since they've licensed a Korean game, should they hire a few Koreans as low-level managers?"

Wang Zijie smiled without saying a word, looking at Chen Tianqiao as if he were an idiot.

Korean companies have always been mercenary, and Shanda wasn't the only one they screwed over.

Don't be fooled by 9you's current glory from licensing *Audition Online*. In less than a year, they'd be backstabbed. The Korean side would collude with The9 to extort 9you, leading to 9you spending 45 million USD to settle and renew the contract, while The9 smoothly secured the rights to *Audition Online 2*.

That whole ordeal torpedoed 9you's plans to go public.

IDG also got screwed over badly, unable to cash out its 9you shares through an IPO.

Why did Koreans have no fear when facing Chinese people? It was because no matter how arrogant and disgusting they were, there were always Chinese publishers desperately kissing up to them. Chinese publishers would even backstab each other, proactively raising licensing fees and letting the Korean developers reap the rewards.

Chen Tianqiao pointed at Park Heon-joo and said sternly, "There is no scientific proof that Chinese people are idiots. You must apologize to all Chinese people!"

The camera from Dragon TV also panned over.

Seeing that he had angered the crowd, Park Heon-joo started to deny it. "I never said such things. The few of you are ganging up to frame me. You are the ones who should apologize, or I will sue you for slander."

Everyone at Park Heon-joo's table, including the moderator, was left speechless by the Korean.

He was denying words he had just spoken moments ago.

Zhang Chun from Object Software said, "I heard him say it with my own ears."

Liu Kun from Pixel Soft also said, "I heard it too."

Both of them developed their own games and weren't the least bit afraid of offending the Koreans.

Wang Zijie weighed the pros and cons, felt that it wouldn't cause any major issues, and followed up, "I heard it too."

Only Yang Jin from Yangcheng Gnetwork was left. He could only say, "I heard it."

With a unanimous consensus, everyone pretty much understood the situation.

Park Heon-joo was still playing dumb. "I never said it! You're ganging up to slander me! You have ill intentions towards me. I refuse to participate in any further activities."

With that, the guy just left.

He even ran outside and told the Ourgame employees who were setting up the exhibition booth to pack up and withdraw from this year's convention.

A very bewildering move.

The CCTV reporter extended a microphone. "Mr. Chen, can you elaborate on what just happened?"

The reporter from Dragon TV also quickly offered a microphone.

Facing two microphones and two cameras, Chen Tianqiao recounted the events with righteous indignation, concluding with a stirring declaration, "This is infuriating, a tremendous humiliation. The company under my name will never, ever rely on Korean games to make money. I've said it today, and I'll stand by my word. I will do as I say!"

Hearing this, his peers all smiled.

First, because Chen Tianqiao had berated a Korean, which was very cathartic for them.

Second, if Chen Tianqiao wasn't going to license Korean online games, they would have one less competitor in the future.

However, Chen Tianqiao only said he wouldn't rely on Korean games to make money; he didn't say he wouldn't negotiate licensing with Korean developers.

He could still totally negotiate for *DNF*, giving the Korean side the illusion that they could continue to drive up the price.

If he wanted to be shameless, he could even sign for *DNF*: pay only 30% of the licensing fee upon signing, and then drag his feet on the second payment during the technology transfer phase. He could delay the Korean side for several months. Only after the technology transfer deadline in the contract passed could Qu Li unilaterally terminate the contract and go negotiate with other publishers. And Chen Tianqiao's loss would only be that 30% of the licensing fee.

But doing so would be too damaging to one's reputation and credibility. Chen Tianqiao wouldn't stoop that low.

The Dragon TV reporter asked, "Will Game Science only operate self-developed games from now on?"

Chen Tianqiao said, "Being completely closed off will only make one fall behind. I will definitely cooperate with other countries, but Korean developers are excluded. Of course, Game Science will focus on self-developed games. *Legends of the Three Kingdoms* is operating very well right now, with a daily active user count of about 250,000."

"Such high daily active users?" a reporter from PCgames.com.cn asked in surprise.

Chen Tianqiao smiled and said, "That's because the vast majority of *Legends of the Three Kingdoms* users have their own computers, instead of going to internet cafes to play games. During their breaks from study or work, they will always log in to play a couple of rounds."

It was now impossible to calculate the registered users for *Legends of the Three Kingdoms*, because accounts on the Youke-Uu Platform were interconnected.

Youke accounts registered because of *Happy Farm* could also log directly into *Legends of the Three Kingdoms*. And there really were some uncles and aunties who, in between stealing crops, playing Landlords, and playing Tetris, would curiously download the *Legends of the Three Kingdoms* client.

Ding Lei was also quite surprised and looked at the person next to him, Chen Guiliang. "He can reach 250,000 daily active users without going through internet cafes?"

"That's pretty impressive," said Chen Guiliang.

Ding Lei asked, "Have you played that game?"

Qu Li Jing shook her head. "No."

The 17173 reporter asked, "CEO Chen, after the summit is over, could we do an exclusive interview with you?"

"Of course, you can." An exclusive interview was exactly what Chen Tianqiao was waiting for.
